newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan blames China for Pretoria decision on ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan blames China for Pretoria decision on ties.

text.p: Taiwanese officials on Thursday blamed China for South Africa's decision to sever ties in favour of Beijing, saying China was "buying" foreign ties and damaging chances for reunification between the longtime rivals.
"The origin of this issue is communist China," government spokesman Su Chi quoted Premier Lien Chan as saying after a morning cabinet meeting.

"This shows communist China is intensifying its repression of us internationally. Its moves to buy foreign relations will not do any good to cross-strait relations or national reunification," Lien was quoted as saying.
South African President Nelson Mandela told reporters in Johannesburg on Wednesday that Pretoria would switch diplomatic ties from Taipei to Beijing by the end of 1997.
Taiwan and China have been separated since a civil war ended in 1949. Both governments say they want reunification but refuse even to talk to each other about how to achieve it.
China sees Taiwan as a Chinese province not entitled to foreign ties while Taiwan insists its 21 million people have a right not to be excluded from international activities.
South Africa is the biggest of just 30 states that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China rather than the communist People's Republic on the mainland.

"We can only say that communist China has no intention to develop bilateral relations in a smooth direction," said Chan Chih-hung, a director of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, Taiwan's top China policymaking body.
There were no protests at Pretoria's embassy, a contrast with the public outrage displayed in recent years after Washington, Seoul and other erstwhile allies dropped Taipei for Beijing.
The switch even took Pretoria's Taipei envoy by surprise.
"I am sad at the moment," ambassador Johannes Viljoen told reporters after being summoned by foreign minister John Chang on Thursday. "I was not informed beforehand by my government,"
Viljoen urged Taiwan not to exact reprisals against Pretoria while Chang said Taipei would conduct an overall review of billions of dollars in Taiwan investments in South Africa.
